docs.title: Open interest
docs.text: The number of option contracts at one strike that are currently held by someone. High open interest means a lot of money already has a position at that price.

docs.title: Wall
docs.text: A strike carrying so much open interest that price tends to slow down, stall or turn when it gets there. Red walls sit above price, green walls below.

docs.title: ATM, OTM, ITM
docs.text: At the money means the strike is roughly where the stock is trading. Out of the money means it still needs to move for the option to be worth anything at expiry. In the money means it already is.

docs.title: DTE
docs.text: Days to expiration - how many days are left before the option expires. Fewer days means faster moves in the option's price, in both directions.

docs.title: Delta
docs.text: Roughly how much the option's price moves for a one dollar move in the stock. A delta of 0.30 means about thirty cents per dollar.

docs.title: Expected move
docs.text: How far the options market is pricing the stock to travel by expiry, up or down. It is a range, not a prediction of direction.

docs.title: VWAP
docs.text: Volume-weighted average price - the average price paid today, weighted by how much traded at each level. Price above it usually means buyers are in control.

docs.title: EMA and SMA
docs.text: Moving averages, which smooth price into a line. An EMA reacts faster to recent moves than an SMA of the same length.

docs.title: RVOL
docs.text: Relative volume - how much is trading now compared with what is normal for this stock at this time of day. Above one means busier than usual.

docs.title: Squeeze
docs.text: A period where a stock's range tightens and pressure builds. When the squeeze fires, that pressure releases and a larger move often follows.

docs.title: Skittles
docs.text: A fast momentum reading between 0 and 100, coloured by which way the trend is running. High and green means momentum is stretched upward.

docs.title: Regular and extended hours
docs.text: Regular hours run 9:30 AM to 4:00 PM ET. Extended hours are the trading before and after that, where far fewer people are active and moves are less reliable.

docs.title: 5-minute close confirmation
docs.text: Waiting for a full five-minute candle to finish above or below a level before treating it as broken. It filters out brief spikes that immediately reverse.

docs.title: Find something moving
docs.text: Trading starts with a shortlist, not a chart. AGX gives you two ways to build one. Premarket watches nine large-cap names every trading morning between 6:00 and 9:30 AM ET and tells you which are waking up before the bell. MomX Scanner is the wider net: a few hundred names scored the same way, refreshed every minute, all day. Start with Premarket in the morning. Switch to MomX once the market is open.

docs.title: Put it on a chart
docs.text: Type a ticker at the top of the chart, pick a timeframe, and pick how many charts you want on screen at once. You can show anything from a single chart up to ten at a time, and there is a MAG7 layout that puts all seven big names side by side. Most people start with one chart on the 5-minute and add more later.

docs.title: Read the trend
docs.text: Your chart already has five lines on it before you touch anything: three exponential moving averages at 9, 21 and 50 bars, a 200-bar simple moving average, and VWAP, the volume-weighted average price. The short reading: when the faster lines sit above the slower ones and price sits above VWAP, buyers are in control on that timeframe. When they cross back the other way, that control is changing hands. Underneath the candles are two more panels showing the same question answered across several timeframes at once, so you can see whether the 5-minute move agrees with the hourly one.

docs.title: See where price is likely to stall
docs.text: The red and green horizontal bands across the chart are option walls. Red bands sit above price where large numbers of call contracts are open; green bands sit below where large numbers of puts are. These are the prices where a lot of money has already taken a position, so price often slows down, stalls, or reverses when it reaches one. They are not guarantees. They are the levels worth knowing about before you enter.

docs.title: Check the option itself
docs.text: A good chart setup can still be a bad option. The Options page shows you the contract, not just the stock. For each strike you get how many days are left, its delta, how much volume and open interest it carries, and how that compares with the at-the-money strike. The expected move tells you roughly how far the stock is priced to travel before expiry. What you are looking for is a strike with real activity in it, close enough to the money to respond when the stock moves.

docs.title: Let the app watch it for you
docs.text: You cannot stare at nine charts at once, so hand the watching over. Every trading morning at 9:15 AM ET, AGX builds a ladder of the biggest call strikes above the price and the biggest put strikes below it, then tells you when price actually confirms through one. MAG7 is watched by default, and you can add your own tickers. You can also draw your own alert on any chart by clicking a price. It snaps to whatever level it lands on, so the alert is named after the thing you cared about.

docs.title: Save your setup
docs.text: Once a chart looks the way you want it, save it. Your indicator choices can be saved for every ticker on that timeframe at once, so you set up the 5-minute chart once and every symbol you open inherits it. Your watchlist is shared across the scanners and the chart, so a ticker you save in one place shows up in the others.

docs.title: Let it find you: the Momo Alert
docs.text: You do not have to watch the scanner. When a stock's volume suddenly runs times its normal - while the momentum scan passes - a MOMO banner and sound interrupt whatever panel you are on. That sudden-volume-plus-momentum combination is what the start of a real move looks like. Set it up once: on the MomX board, open the gear next to refresh, tick the timeframes you want watched, and set how unusual volume must be before it interrupts you. It alerts once per ticker per 15 minutes, and your settings are yours alone. To get the same alerts on your phone - locked, in your pocket, browser closed - install the free ntfy app, tap Generate under Phone push in that same gear window, and subscribe to the generated name in the app. The full walkthrough is in the Setup tab at the top of this page.

docs.title: Charts
docs.text: A chart is one ticker's price history drawn as candles. Each candle covers a fixed slice of time and shows four things: where price opened, where it closed, and the highest and lowest it reached in between. The same stock tells a different story depending on the slice you choose. A 5-minute chart shows you today's fight; a daily chart shows you the trend that fight sits inside. Reading both is the point of having eleven timeframes rather than one.

docs.title: Charts: Timeframes
docs.text: 3m, 5m, 10m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 4h, D (daily), W (weekly) and M (monthly). A common habit: check the 4-hour and daily for direction, then drop to the 5-minute to time the entry. If those disagree, the trade is a fight, not a trend.

docs.title: Charts: Charts on screen at once
docs.text: Single, 2 side by side, 2 stacked, 3 across, 3 grid, 3 stacked, 4 grid, 4 across, 4 stacked, 6 grid, 6 across, 7 across, 8 across, MAG7, 8 grid, 9 grid and 10 grid. Ten panels is the most you can have open at one time. MAG7 puts all seven big names in a single row. In the one-row layouts the column dividers can be dragged, and every panel keeps its own ticker and its own timeframe.

docs.title: Charts: Drawing on the chart
docs.text: Crosshair: The default. Move the pointer to read any candle's values, and drag to move the chart. Select: Pick up a drawing you already made, to move it, restyle it or delete it. Trend line: A sloped line between two points, for drawing the path a move has been following. Horizontal line: A flat line at one price, for marking a level you care about. Fibonacci retracement: Drag across a move to mark the levels a pullback commonly stops at. Rectangle: Box off a zone rather than a single price, such as a consolidation range. Brush: Freehand drawing, for when a shape matters more than precision. Text note: Type a note directly on the chart so you remember why you marked something. Price and time measure: Drag from one point to another to read the distance in both price and time.

docs.title: Charts: Before the bell and after it
docs.text: Shaded areas mark pre-market and after-hours trading. Candles exist there, but far fewer people are trading, so moves can be larger and less reliable than they look. Vertical session lines mark the times of day that matter, so you can see at a glance where the open and the close fall inside all those candles.

docs.title: Charts: Saving what you set up
docs.text: The save buttons are named after the timeframe you are standing on, so on a 5-minute chart they read Save 5m for all tickers and Save 5m chart layout. Your panel arrangement and each panel's ticker and timeframe are kept for you automatically, so neither button is about those. Save 5m for all tickers applies your indicator choices to every symbol you open on the 5-minute, so you configure that timeframe once rather than once per ticker. Save 5m chart layout remembers the framing instead: how far back the chart is zoomed, where the latest candle sits, and how tall the lower panes are. Reset 5m puts that timeframe back to how it arrived.

docs.title: Charts: Linking and popping out
docs.text: The coloured link buttons tie surfaces together: set two of them to the same colour and changing the ticker in one changes it in the other. Set them to different colours to keep two tickers side by side without them following each other. Any chart can be popped out into its own window, which is how you fill a second monitor. The pop-out keeps its link colour, so it can still follow the main screen.

docs.title: Indicators and studies
docs.text: An indicator is a second opinion drawn on top of price. It does not know anything price does not; it re-arranges what already happened so a pattern is easier to see - a smoothed average, a measure of how compressed the range has got, a marker where two averages crossed. More is not better. Every study you switch on is another voice, and a chart with thirty voices tells you nothing. The set that is already on when you arrive is deliberately small; add to it only when you know what question the new study answers.

docs.title: Indicators and studies: What is already on when you arrive
docs.text: EMA 9, EMA 21, EMA 50: Three fast-to-slow moving averages, drawn magenta, yellow and cyan. Their order tells you who is winning: fastest on top is buyers, fastest on the bottom is sellers. SMA 200: A slow dark-green average used as the long-run line in the sand. Price above it is a market in an uptrend on that timeframe. VWAP: The white line: the average price actually paid today, weighted by size. Large funds measure their fills against it, which is why price so often returns to it. OI levels / High OI: The red and green horizontal bands. These are the option strikes carrying the most open contracts above and below price. EMA clouds: Shading between the 9 and 21 averages, and between the 21 and 50. A thick cloud is a strong trend; a flat, thin one is chop. MTF 4x8 one-sided clouds: The same cloud idea computed on several higher timeframes at once, so a 5-minute chart can show you what the hourly is doing. Ichimoku: A Japanese trend system: two fast lines, a forward-projected cloud that acts as support or resistance, and a lagging line confirming the move. Signal labels: The CALL and PUT tags printed on the candles when a momentum cross fires on one of the higher timeframes. MTF MA levels: Flat lines carrying the daily, weekly and monthly moving averages onto whatever timeframe you are looking at. Session lines and previous day, week and month levels: Vertical markers for the times of day that matter, plus the prior period's open, high, low and close - the levels most traders are watching. Candle colours: The cyan and magenta candle scheme, so a candle's own colour already carries the short-term momentum reading. The three lower panels: Under the candles: trend strength across timeframes, a written label of what each timeframe's cloud is doing, and a squeeze grid showing where pressure is building.

docs.title: Indicators and studies: Trend lines
docs.text: EMA 9 / EMA 21 / EMA 50: Exponential moving averages. They weight recent bars more heavily, so they turn sooner than a simple average of the same length. SMA 200: A simple 200-bar average - every bar counts the same. Slow, but it is the line the largest number of people are watching. VWAP: Volume-weighted average price, reset each session. Above it buyers are paying up; below it sellers are.

docs.title: Indicators and studies: Clouds
docs.text: EMA Clouds: Shading between 9/21 and between 21/50. Colour tells you direction, thickness tells you conviction. MTF 4x8 One-Sided Clouds: A 4-versus-8 crossover cloud drawn for the current timeframe and every higher one up to 4 hours. MTF MACD 6/12/8 Trend Clouds: A momentum cloud that needs both a MACD zero-cross and an EMA 9/20 confirmation before it changes colour. MTF EMA 9x20 Signal Clouds: The 9-versus-20 crossover cloud, drawn across several timeframes at once. MTF Squeeze Release Clouds: Clouds plus bubbles marking where a squeeze released, on every timeframe up to daily. Cloud Bands: One fixed timeframe's cloud pinned onto your chart. There is a separate switch for 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 4h and daily. CloudMAX MTF EMA 1/5/15: A denser cloud set with arrows and bubbles, for reading fast intraday turns.

docs.title: Indicators and studies: Signal labels
docs.text: Call & Put Signals 4x8: Yellow CALL and magenta PUT tags from the 4-versus-8 cross, read on the 5-minute through 4-hour timeframes. Call & Put Signals 9x20: The same idea from the 9-versus-20 cross, in cyan and magenta, read on the 30-minute through 4-hour timeframes. 4x8 Daily to Monthly signals: The slow version of the 4-versus-8 cross: daily, 2-day, 3-day, 4-day, weekly and monthly, each one waiting on the next timeframe up to confirm it. 9x20 Daily to Monthly signals: The 9-versus-20 cross on those same six slow aggregations, printed on the first chart candle of the day it belongs to. MACD Daily to Monthly signals: MACD 6/12/8 crosses on the slow aggregations, for when you want a momentum read rather than a moving-average one.

docs.title: Indicators and studies: Lower panels
docs.text: MTF ADX Clouds: Trend strength, not direction. It answers whether anything is actually trending here, across the current timeframe and five higher ones. Squeeze Momentum: The classic squeeze histogram: dots show when the range is compressed, and the bars show which way the pressure is leaning. MTF Cloud Label: A written row per timeframe saying whether that timeframe's cloud is bullish or bearish, from 5-minute up to weekly. MTF Squeeze 4/10: Eight squeeze rows in their own pane, so you can see at a glance which timeframes are coiled and which have already fired.

docs.title: Indicators and studies: Levels
docs.text: OI Levels / High OI: Full-width call-resistance and put-support bands from the expiry you have selected. PivotPoints and PersonsPivots: Two classic pivot systems that project support and resistance from the previous period's range. MTF MA Levels: Daily, weekly and monthly moving averages carried onto the chart you are on as flat lines. Previous D/W/M OHLC: Yesterday's, last week's and last month's open, high, low and close - each period can be switched on separately. Session Time Lines: Vertical Eastern-time markers for the session boundaries. Extended Sessions: Shading behind the pre-market and after-hours candles so you can tell them apart at a glance. AutoFib: Draws the 38.2%, 50% and 61.8% retracement zone of the current swing for you, without you dragging anything. Big swing Fib: On Daily, Weekly and Monthly charts: Fib levels from the lowest low to the highest high of the last year, two years or five years, with the 50% to 61.8% zone shaded, like a TradingView Fib drawn by hand. Relative Volume Candles: Prints a small relative-volume number under each candle, so an unusually heavy bar stands out. TOS candle colours: The reference candle colouring, so a candle's body already tells you the short-term momentum state.

docs.title: Indicators and studies: Turning one on and saving it
docs.text: Open the indicators panel from the chart toolbar. Every study is a checkbox; ticking it draws it immediately. Expanding a row gives you its settings - period lengths on the moving averages, colours, and which timeframes a multi-timeframe study should include. Then save, or you will do this again tomorrow. Save 5m for all tickers writes the whole set as your profile for that timeframe, so every symbol you open on the 5-minute inherits it. Reset 5m throws your changes away and puts the starting set back. On another timeframe the buttons are named after that one instead.

docs.title: Options and open interest
docs.text: An option contract gives its holder the right to buy (a call) or sell (a put) 100 shares at a fixed price, called the strike, until a fixed date. Open interest is simply how many of those contracts at one strike are currently held by somebody and not yet closed. That matters because open interest is money already committed at a specific price. When a strike carries a very large amount of it, the traders on the other side of those contracts have to hedge as price approaches - so price tends to be pulled toward the strike, and then to stall there. A strike like that is what this app calls a wall. Walls are not predictions. They are the prices where something is likely to happen: a stall, a squeeze through, or a reversal. Knowing where the next one sits before you enter is most of the value.

docs.title: Options and open interest: Finding your way around the board
docs.text: The Options board has a row of tabs across the top: Chain, Heatmap, Flow, C/P Levels and News. It opens on Chain, the strike-by-strike table for one expiry. Inside Chain there is a second, smaller pair of tabs: Chain and High OI. That pair opens on High OI, which ranks the out-of-the-money strikes that carry real size - the read most people open a ticker for. Switch to the inner Chain tab when you want to compare neighbouring strikes rather than only the crowded ones. Whichever of the two you leave it on is remembered, so the app does not fight you next time.

docs.title: Options and open interest: The C/P Levels banner
docs.text: The strike-by-strike read described below lives on a different top-row tab: C/P Levels. Open that, and this banner appears above the tables. LIVE shows the current price with today's change. ATM STRIKE is the strike sitting closest to that price - at the money. EXP RANGE is the expected move: the distance the options market is currently pricing the stock to travel by expiry, shown as a low-to-high band around the price. Read the expected range as a boundary, not a forecast. It says nothing about direction - only that a move beyond that band would be larger than what is currently priced in. Below it, CALL ATM and PUT ATM give you the at-the-money strike on each side with its volume and its open interest, so you can see immediately whether today's activity is going into calls or into puts.

docs.title: Options and open interest: What each column means on C/P Levels
docs.text: OTM Strike: The out-of-the-money strike this row is about - above price for calls, below price for puts. Exp Move: The expected move in dollars for this expiry: how far the stock is priced to travel before it expires. DTE: Days to expiration, with the actual expiry date underneath. Fewer days means faster moves in the option's price, in both directions. Delta: Roughly how much this option's price moves per one dollar move in the stock. 0.30 means about thirty cents. OTM Vol: How many contracts traded at this strike today. Volume is today's activity, and it resets every session. OTM OI: How many contracts are still held open at this strike. Open interest is the accumulated position, and it is reported once a day rather than tick by tick. Vol/OI: Today's volume divided by the existing open interest. A high number means today's traders are piling into a strike that was quiet, which is new positioning rather than old. ATM Strike: The at-the-money strike being compared against, so you can judge this row without leaving the row. ATM Vol: Today's contract volume at that at-the-money strike. ATM OI: Open contracts held at that at-the-money strike. Flow Type: Whether this row's case rests on today's volume or on the standing open interest. Volume-led is fresh; open-interest-led is established. Liquidity Winner: Which of the two strikes is actually getting the money right now - this out-of-the-money strike, or the at-the-money one. Setup Type: A short description of the shape the row forms, so you can scan for the pattern you trade instead of reading every number. Scanner Tag: The label the scan attached to this row, naming why it was worth surfacing. Strength: A 0-100 score combining the above into one bar, so the strongest rows sort to the top. Treat it as a shortlist, not a verdict.

docs.title: Options and open interest: Strong, moderate, weak
docs.text: Strikes that qualify as walls carry a HIGH OI badge reading STRONG, MOD or WEAK. The grade is this strike's open interest measured against the biggest wall on its own side: two-thirds or more of the leader is STRONG, a third or more is MOD, and below that is WEAK. So MOD does not mean a weak strike, it means one standing behind the leader - and more than one STRONG wall on the same side is normal when two strikes are carrying comparable size. It is the same grading the chart uses to draw its red and green bands, so a STRONG badge here is the band you can already see on the chart, not a second opinion about it.

docs.title: Options and open interest: The colour key
docs.text: Call wall - resistance above price Put wall - support below price

docs.title: Options and open interest: The tags on a strike row
docs.text: CALL ITM: Marks the call side that is already in the money - the stock has passed above that strike. PUT ITM: The same on the put side: price has fallen through that strike. ATM: Highlights the strike nearest the current price, the pivot the whole board is measured against. HIGH OI: A wall strike, carried with its STRONG, MOD or WEAK grade. EM HIGH: The top of the expected-move range: a move above this is larger than the options market has priced in. EM LOW: The bottom of that same expected-move range.

docs.title: Options and open interest: Taking the levels elsewhere
docs.text: If you also chart in thinkorswim or TradingView, the OI Level Scripts page turns the top call and put open-interest levels for one expiry into a study you can paste straight into either platform, so the same lines appear there. The script is generated from the option chain at the moment you press the button, so regenerate it once the chain has moved on.

docs.title: Alerts
docs.text: An alert is the app watching a price line so you do not have to. You cannot hold nine tickers and their levels in your head at once, and the moment you look away is the moment one of them moves. There are two kinds here. The automatic ladder builds itself every trading morning from the option open interest, and tells you when price reaches the levels that matter. Manual alerts are the ones you draw yourself, on any price you care about.

docs.title: Alerts: The morning ladder
docs.text: At 9:15 AM ET on every trading day, the app builds a ladder for each watched ticker: the biggest call strikes stacked above the current price, and the biggest put strikes stacked below it. That is the plan for the day. The seven big names - AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, AMZN, META, GOOGL and TSLA - are watched by default, and you can type any other ticker into the add box to have a ladder built for it too. Each card shows the ticker's price, the level it is working on now, and the one after that.

docs.title: Alerts: Touched versus CONFIRMED
docs.text: Touched: Price has reached the level with a wick but has not held there. This is an early warning only: it tells you the level is live right now, and the ladder does not move on. A touch fires once per level, so it cannot spam you. CONFIRMED: A complete 5-minute candle has closed through the level. That is the event the app treats as real, because a close through a price is a decision, while a wick through it is often a test that failed. The next target: As soon as a level confirms, the ladder advances and the message names the next strike above or below, how much open interest it carries, and how far away it is in both dollars and percent.

docs.title: Alerts: What the message tells you
docs.text: A confirmation reads like this: the ticker, an arrow for direction, the side and the strike or strikes that were taken out, the word CONFIRMED, the 5-minute closing price that did it, and then the next target with its size and distance. If price closed through two levels in one candle, both are named. A touch message says so plainly instead, and states what would be needed to confirm - a 5-minute close above the strike for a call level, below it for a put level. Once a side has confirmed for the day it goes quiet until you re-arm it, so a level that has already gone does not keep shouting.

docs.title: Alerts: Alerts you draw yourself
docs.text: On any chart, use the bell button or click the price you care about. If your click lands within a few pixels of a level the chart is already drawing, the alert snaps to it and takes its name - so you get previous day high, or High OI, rather than a bare number you will not recognise a week later. Armed alerts appear as chips on the price axis, at the price they are watching. Tapping a strike on the option board also starts one, pre-set to fire upward if the strike is above the price and downward if it is below. The live price and existing alert chips are deliberately not snap targets: snapping to the live price would create an alert that fires the instant you made it.

docs.title: Alerts: Sound and notifications
docs.text: Alerts on is the master switch, and MAG7 controls whether the seven big names are included. Enable sound asks your browser for permission to show notifications, and turns on the alert tone. Once granted the button reads Sound on, and clicking it again plays a test tone so you can check your volume before the market opens. If your browser refuses notifications you still get the tone, and the button says Sound only.

docs.title: Scanner (premarket)
docs.text: Before the bell the question is short: of the big names, which one is actually waking up? Overnight ranges are thin and most of what happens is noise, so this board is deliberately narrow - nine tickers, one window, one score. It does not try to find you a stock you have never heard of. It tells you which of the names you were going to trade anyway has momentum behind it this morning, so you know where to point your first chart at 9:30.

docs.title: Scanner (premarket): The window and the names
docs.text: The scan runs between 6:00 and 9:30 AM ET on trading days. Outside that window the board is quiet, and that is expected rather than broken - there is nothing pre-market about the middle of the afternoon. The nine names are AAPL, AMZN, AVGO, GOOGL, META, MSFT, NFLX, NVDA and TSLA. The list is fixed: it is the set the scanner is built around, and their tapes are kept warm so the board can read them whether or not you have a chart open.

docs.title: Scanner (premarket): What the signals mean
docs.text: CALL2H: A bullish momentum cross that has fired on the 2-hour view of the tape - the shorter of the two confirmations. CALL4H: The same cross on the 4-hour view. Slower to appear and harder to earn, so it carries more weight than the 2-hour on its own. Why it agrees with your chart: These are not a second calculation. They are read from the same study that draws the CALL and PUT labels on your chart, so the board and the chart cannot tell you different things about the same morning.

docs.title: Scanner (premarket): Squeeze fires
docs.text: A squeeze is a stretch where a stock's range tightens and pressure builds; when it releases, a larger move often follows. The board counts squeeze fires on the 1-hour, 2-hour, 4-hour and Daily views. 15-minute and 30-minute squeezes are deliberately left out. They fire almost continuously, so including them would add a hit to nearly every ticker every morning and drown the score in noise rather than sharpening it.

docs.title: Scanner (premarket): The four numbers at the top
docs.text: MATCHES: How many of the nine tickers cleared the scan this morning, with the scan window printed underneath it. STRONG: How many matches are graded strong. The grade is about the quality of the crosses, not how many hits a row has: the cyan 9x20 cross outranks the yellow 4x8 one, so a cyan and a yellow together, or two cyan, is STRONG; a single cyan or two yellow is MODERATE; one yellow alone is WEAK. A row carrying only squeeze fires never reaches STRONG, because a release says a move is coming without saying which way - though two or more fires do lift a row that already has a cross. Live tapes: How many of the nine have usable data for today. This is the honesty number: a ticker with no data today cannot be scanned, and the note names it rather than quietly reporting no setups. FEED: Whether this morning's data arrived complete or with a hole in it. GAP means part of the pre-market window is missing, so treat the 2-hour and 4-hour reads as partial.

docs.title: Scanner (premarket): The morning briefing
docs.text: Underneath the board, the briefing is a short written summary of the morning: which tickers matched, what fired on each, and what the shape of the session looks like going into the open. It is saved with the day, so tomorrow you can read what yesterday's board was actually saying rather than trying to reconstruct it from the numbers.

docs.title: Scanner (premarket): Looking back
docs.text: The last 30 mornings are kept, and you can read them three ways. Table gives you one day at a time with arrows to step backward and forward. Calendar lays the month out so you can see which mornings were busy at a glance. List runs everything together for scanning quickly. This is the fastest way to learn whether a signal is worth anything to you: find the mornings a ticker matched, then look at what the day did afterwards.

docs.title: MomX Scanner
docs.text: MomX is the wide board. Where the pre-market Scanner watches nine names closely, this one scores a few hundred the same way every minute and shows you the ones that pass, all day. Every row on it has already cleared the same filter, so the board is a shortlist rather than a market. Your job reading it is to choose between candidates, not to decide whether they qualify.

docs.title: MomX Scanner: What a row has to do to appear
docs.text: Three requirements must all be true. The stock trades at $3 or more. Its 4-hour volume is up at least 0.5% against two bars ago. Its 1-hour price is up at least 0.3% against two bars ago. Then at least one thing has to actually be happening: a momentum cross on one of the tracked timeframes, a squeeze that has just fired, or a relative-volume hit. Clear the three requirements but show none of those three, and the name stays off the board. Every reason a row passed is kept, not only the first one, so a name showing four reasons genuinely has four things going for it.

docs.title: MomX Scanner: Reading the board left to right
docs.text: Industry, Symbol, % Chg, then the 1D sparkline. Next a first block of RVOL - 2h, 4h and D - then H/L, then a second RVOL block at 5, 15, 30 and 1h. After the thin separator column come the squeeze columns at 2h, 4h, D and W, then Skittles at 2h and 4h, then Quote, then the slow Skittles: D, 2D, 3D, 4D, W and Mo. The RVOL block being split by H/L, and the Skittles block by Quote, is not an accident of layout. This board is a replay of the scan window it was built to mirror, column for column, so it is laid out the way that window is.

docs.title: MomX Scanner: What each column means
docs.text: Industry: The sector the name belongs to. Three or four rows from the same industry at once is usually the real story, not three separate ones. % Chg: How far the stock has moved today, in percent. 1D: A miniature chart of the day's shape, so you can tell a steady climb from a spike that has already faded without opening the chart. RVOL: Relative volume: how much is trading now against what is normal for this stock at this time of day. Above 1 is busier than usual; the short timeframes catch a burst, the long ones tell you whether it has lasted. H/L: Where price is sitting inside the recent range, drawn as a fill rather than a number. It reads the last 8 two-hour bars with extended hours on - roughly 16 hours, not just today. Full means price is at the top of that range; EMPTY means the MIDDLE of it, not the bottom. Below the middle the bar fills the other way and turns red. Squeeze: Pressure building and then releasing. A squeeze column tells you that timeframe's range has compressed, and changes when it fires. The separator column: A thin solid stripe with no data in it, there only to break the volume block away from the pressure block so your eye does not slide across them. Skittles: A fast 0-100 momentum reading, coloured by which way the trend is running. The short columns are today's push; the daily-to-monthly ones tell you whether it fits a bigger move. Quote: The quote trend: the last few bars up or down as a tiny bar chart, so you get the immediate direction at a glance without reading a number.

docs.title: MomX Scanner: How often it refreshes
docs.text: The board rebuilds every 60 seconds. That pace is deliberate: scoring a few hundred names is real work, and asking for it more often would make the app slower without telling you anything new. While a refresh is in flight, the last board you saw stays on screen rather than blanking. A board that looks unchanged for a moment is normal - the build time is what tells you how fresh it is.

docs.title: MomX Scanner: Your own lists
docs.text: The tabs above the board are lists. Switch between them to score a different universe, and the tab you were last on is remembered when you come back. The Tickers box replaces the active list: paste or type the symbols you want, press Set, and the next build scores those instead. A list that has just been changed shows as building until its first full board lands.

docs.title: MomX Scanner: The Momo Alert
docs.text: This board can also interrupt you: the amber MOMO banner, its sound, and the push that reaches your phone even locked. It is set up once from the gear button next to refresh - the full walkthrough now lives on the Setup tab at the top of this page.

docs.title: TOS API key setup
docs.text: This is optional. Without it, everything in AGX already works on the app's shared data. Do this only if you want your charts and option chains running on your own Schwab account (Schwab is the company behind thinkorswim - same login). It has two parts: first you get two codes from Schwab's website, then you paste them into AGX. The only slow part is Schwab: they take a few days to approve new apps.

docs.title: TOS API key setup: What you need before you start
docs.text: Your Schwab (or thinkorswim) username and password. A computer - this part is easier with a mouse than a phone. About ten minutes now, then a few days of waiting for Schwab's approval.

docs.title: TOS API key setup: Part A - get your two codes from Schwab
docs.text: 1: Open a new browser tab and type this address exactly: developer.schwab.com 2: Click Sign In at the top right, and log in with the SAME username and password you use for Schwab or thinkorswim. 3: The first visit asks you to finish a short developer profile. Where it asks what kind of developer you are, choose Individual. 4: On your dashboard, find the button named Create App and click it. 5: In the form: choose the API product that mentions Market Data, and where it asks for a Callback URL, type exactly: https://127.0.0.1 - then submit the form. No slash on the end: Schwab matches this string exactly against what the app sends. 6: Now you wait. Schwab checks new apps by hand and it usually takes a few days. When your dashboard shows the app as Ready For Use, come back here and continue. 7: Open your approved app on that dashboard. You will see two long codes: an App Key and a Secret. Leave this tab open - you are about to copy both.

docs.title: TOS API key setup: Part B - paste the codes into AGX
docs.text: 1: In AGX on your phone, tap More at the bottom right, then tap the Settings tile (the gear). On a computer, click Settings in the menu. 2: Scroll down until you see the card titled Connect your personal Market Data app. The picture above is that card. 3: Click inside the box labeled MARKET DATA APP KEY and paste the App Key from your Schwab tab. 4: Click the box labeled MARKET DATA APP SECRET and paste the Secret. 5: Press the Save keys button. 6: Press Authenticate Market Data. A Schwab window opens: log in and press Allow. 7: You will land on a page that looks broken - the address starts with 127.0.0.1. That is expected and correct. Copy the ENTIRE address from the address bar. 8: Back in AGX, paste that address into the box labeled MARKET DATA CALLBACK URL and press the Complete button under it.

docs.title: TOS API key setup: You are done when...
docs.text: The card shows a green Authenticated badge next to Market Data, and Test Market Data comes back happy. Your charts, option chains and live stream now run on your own Schwab connection. One thing to expect: about once a week Schwab expires the connection and the app will ask you to repeat Part B steps 6 to 8. AGX warns you three days before that happens.

docs.title: Alpaca key setup
docs.text: Also optional, and much quicker - about five minutes, no waiting. An Alpaca key makes the trading features act on YOUR account instead of the shared one, and Alpaca's free account is enough.

docs.title: Alpaca key setup: Part A - get your two codes from Alpaca
docs.text: 1: Open a new browser tab and type this address exactly: app.alpaca.markets - then click Sign Up and create a free account (just an email and a password). 2: After signing in you land on the Paper Trading dashboard - practice money, and exactly the right place to start. 3: On the right side of that dashboard, find the section named API Keys and press Generate. Two codes appear: an API Key ID and a Secret Key. Leave the tab open.

docs.title: Alpaca key setup: Part B - paste the codes into AGX
docs.text: 1: In AGX: tap More at the bottom right, then Settings (on a computer, click Settings in the menu). 2: Scroll to the card titled MY DATA PROVIDER KEYS and find the box named Alpaca Market Data. The picture above is that card. 3: Click the box labeled API KEY ID and paste the API Key ID from your Alpaca tab. 4: Click the box labeled API SECRET and paste the Secret Key. 5: Press Save Alpaca keys.

docs.title: Alpaca key setup: You are done when...
docs.text: The Alpaca Market Data card shows a short piece of your key at its top right instead of Not configured. Trading features now use your own account.

docs.title: Momo Alert setup
docs.text: The Momo Alert watches the scanner for you. When a stock suddenly trades several times its normal volume - while the momentum scan passes - a MOMO banner and a sound interrupt whatever screen you are on. That combination is what the start of a real move looks like. It alerts once per ticker per 15 minutes, only while the market is live, and everything you set here is yours alone - it never changes another user's alerts.

docs.title: Momo Alert setup: Turn it on
docs.text: 1: Open the MomX scanner: tap MomX in the bottom bar (on a computer, MomX Scanner in the menu). 2: In the row of buttons above the table, press the gear - it sits right next to the round refresh arrow. The MOMO ALERT window in the picture above opens. 3: Tick the timeframes you want watched. 5m catches a move the moment volume arrives; 30m, 1h and 2h catch a slower, sustained mover. 4: The number next to each timeframe is how unusual volume must be before it interrupts you: 3 means three times normal. Start with 3; raise it to 4 or 5 if you get too many alerts.

docs.title: Momo Alert setup: Get it on your phone - locked, in your pocket
docs.text: 1: On your phone, open the App Store (or Play Store), search for ntfy, and install it. It is free, with no account and no sign-up. 2: Back in the MOMO ALERT window, under Phone push, press Generate. That creates your private channel name and saves it. The name works like a password - do not share it. 3: Open the ntfy app, tap the + button, choose Subscribe to topic, and type your channel name EXACTLY as AGX shows it. 4: Back in AGX, press Send test next to Generate. Your phone should buzz within a few seconds. If it does not, the name in ntfy and the name in AGX do not match - check them letter by letter, they are case-sensitive. 4: When your phone asks to allow notifications, tap Allow.

docs.title: Momo Alert setup: You are done when...
docs.text: The Send test buzzed your phone, the MOMO ALERT window shows your timeframes ticked, and the ntfy app lists your channel. From now on alerts reach your phone even with the browser closed and the phone locked, because the scanner itself sends them - not this page. Tip: in ntfy you can give the channel its own sound so you know a MOMO buzz without looking.

docs.title: How to check app health
docs.text: AGX runs on one Windows PC and heals itself: anything that stops is restarted within about ten minutes, and the journal, keys and code are copied to Google Drive twice a day. When it still looks wrong, one read-only check tells you which part is down and the exact command to run next - so you never have to guess. Everything here is done at that PC, in PowerShell. Nothing in the check changes anything; it only reads.

docs.title: How to check app health: First, rule out the browser
docs.text: 1: Reload the page hard: Ctrl+F5 on a computer. On the phone close the AGX tab completely and open it again - a tab left open for days keeps an old copy of the app and can show stale lamps. 2: Look at the header lamps. TOS MARKET and TOS TRADING each show the days left on their login; a blinking amber lamp means under two days, EXPIRED means that data source is off until you re-authenticate in Settings. ALPACA red outside market hours is normal. 3: "Unable to sign in" on the login page almost never means a wrong password - it means the app server is down. Go to the next block.

docs.title: How to check app health: Step 1 - the fix that covers almost everything
docs.text: If any port is DOWN, or the login page says it cannot sign you in, paste this and press Enter: Start-ScheduledTask 'AgenticAI-Trading-24x7' Then wait two to three minutes - a cold start is slow - and run Step 0 again. This starts the supervisor that launches and watches every part of the app; if it is already running the command does nothing, so it is always safe.

docs.title: How to check app health: Step 2 - by symptom
docs.text: Error 1033 at app.agxtrade.com: The tunnel to the internet dropped. In a PowerShell opened as Administrator, run: Restart-Service cloudflared . The PC address (127.0.0.1:5173) keeps working the whole time. A TOS lamp blinks or reads EXPIRED: The weekly login ran out. Settings, then the Schwab card, then Authenticate for that app: log in, approve, copy the 127.0.0.1 address from the browser bar, paste it back, Complete. If the PC gets Access Denied from the login page, do the login on your phone over mobile data and paste the address on the PC. Everything OK but no phone alerts: Open the ntfy app and check it is still subscribed to your channel name. Press Send test in the MOMO ALERT window to prove the chain. Backup line says DOWN: Start Google Drive for Desktop from the Start menu, then run: Start-ScheduledTask 'AGX-Nightly-Backup' and check again in five minutes. Until Drive is back, backups land in C:\AGX-Backups on the PC instead. Still wrong after all of this: Copy the whole output of Step 0 and paste it to whoever is helping you - a person or any AI assistant. The full written procedure lives in the docs folder of the app as RUNBOOK.md, and MOVE_TO_NEW_LAPTOP.md covers rebuilding on another machine.

docs.title: How to check app health: What happens on its own
docs.text: Crashed parts restart within ten minutes. Backups run at 1:30 AM and after the close. Your phone gets a push one day before either TOS login expires, and once more if it does expire. None of this needs a developer; the only weekly chore is the TOS re-authentication above.

docs.title: H/L column
docs.text: High/Low: where the price sits inside the last 8 two-hour bars, drawn as a bar. Near +1 is the top of that range and near -1 the bottom. The board is ranked on it.

docs.title: COLOR column
docs.text: A thin coloured separator between the RVOL and SQZ blocks. It carries no number.

docs.title: SQZ column
docs.text: Squeeze on each timeframe: whether the range has tightened, and when the squeeze fired.

docs.title: SKIT column
docs.text: Skittles on each timeframe: a fast momentum reading between 0 and 100, coloured by which way the trend is running.

docs.title: Quote column
docs.text: The quote trend: the last few bars up or down as a tiny bar chart.

docs.title: GO + short RVOL + MACD (calls)
docs.text: BULL, 09:30-15:30 ET: A/A+ with a completed GO breakout, buyers in control on completed 30m candles, a cyan RVOL background on any of 5m/15m/30m, and completed 5m MACD (12,26,9) above its signal with histogram increasing. Checked each refresh; disappears when confirmation no longer passes

docs.title: V2 (calls)
docs.text: at its first A+ or A signal today, from 9:35 AM ET: up less than 10%, momentum Extended, RVOL push. Stays on the list for the day

docs.title: V3 (calls)
docs.text: V2 + a squeeze fired (4h / D / Wk) at that signal

docs.title: Daily 2 (calls)
docs.text: V2 + RVOL push on 2 or more timeframes at that signal, numbered #1, #2, #3 in the order they qualified today

docs.title: G (calls)
docs.text: your rules: RVOL cyan and rising on 30m-D; SQZ 2h/4h fired or none; Skittles 2h cyan cross today after 8 AM + 4h/D cross within 24h; 5m above EMA20 and VWAP or a C5/CALL5 arrow; a strong call-OI wall as target with the ENTRY call's ROI of 150% or more. Exit at the target, at -50% on the option, or at the close

docs.title: Chart CALL2H / CALL4H (calls)
docs.text: the chart printed a CALL2H (last 2 hours) or CALL4H (last 4 hours) arrow - the same arrows as your chart; the time is the chart candle, ET

docs.title: Hot sector leaders (calls)
docs.text: The two strongest stocks (up and above VWAP) of a 🔥 hot sector, fixed when the sector lit (09:35-11:00 ET). CAUTION: in the careful all-day back-test the single #1 stock lost about half the time - the hot sector's GROUP of rising stocks is the reliable signal (45% win, 25% loss), not one name. Best used together with GO / OPT

docs.title: SOLO big-money stocks (calls)
docs.text: Big money in ONE stock (09:45-11:00 ET): volume 5-20x its normal for that time of day, up 1%+, above VWAP and the 09:30 close, $5+, while its sector is not moving. Sep 1-23: 57% ran +4%, but about half gave it back by the close - a fast mover, take profit into strength

docs.title: Best setups in hot sectors (calls)
docs.text: Best setups (GO, or OPT before 10:00) whose industry is a 🔥 HOT sector today - up to 2 sectors, picked between 09:35 and 11:00 ET by one score (how much of it is up and above VWAP + how fast its 3-day lead over SPY is growing). Back-test Sep 1-23: GO in a hot sector won 4 of 6 - a small sample; plain Best setups is the tested everyday choice

docs.title: News + momentum (calls)
docs.text: His order (2026-09-24): the AI reads the news first and finds it POSITIVE (medium or high confidence), then 5m momentum is Building or Extended, then the letter is A+ or A. Not back-tested yet - the AI reads started 2026-09-25

docs.title: Best setups (calls)
docs.text: GO (gap and go, listed first) or OPT (turning up now) when OPT first shows before 10:00 ET. Sep 1-24: 55% win, +0.52% per trade on the stock

docs.title: Gap and go (calls)
docs.text: A+ or A that gapped up 2% or more and, between 09:35 and 10:30, closed a 5m candle above VWAP, the open and the first 5-minute high - with buyers in control on 30m. The META Sept 21 picture

docs.title: Options setup (calls)
docs.text: Before 10:00 ET only. A+ or A with a fresh Skittles cross on BOTH 2h and 4h, buyers in control on 30m (+DI above -DI) and 5m momentum Extended - the META / MRNA picture of Sept 24. Checked live, all day

docs.title: MomoX A+ (calls)
docs.text: MomoX A+ (the MX A+ tag): news in the last 24 hours + RVOL cyan (3+) on any of 15m to D + a squeeze fired, first time today. Bot 2 weeks: lost money (MX A+)

docs.title: Market turn (calls)
docs.text: TURN #n: the market turned UP (SPY back above its VWAP after the morning dip) and this was one of the first stocks to lead the turn. Bot 2 weeks: about breakeven

docs.title: 🔥 Sector leaders (calls)
docs.text: 🔥 Sector leaders: the strongest stocks of today's hot or moving-now sector (up and above VWAP)

docs.title: ZS rule (calls)
docs.text: ZS↑: a 5-minute candle closed ABOVE the EMA 9, 21 and 50, VWAP and the 5m cloud, with nothing in the way within 2% above (day high, premarket high, yesterday's high, pivots). Bot 2 weeks: +7% ROI at middle price, small

docs.title: Short chart arrows (calls)
docs.text: C2H / C4H: the chart's SHORT arrow - the 2-hour or 4-hour trend crossed up while the bigger trend has not turned yet. Market hours only. Bot 2 weeks: +7% ROI at middle price

docs.title: Daily line (calls)
docs.text: LINE↑: the stock opened ABOVE yesterday's high and a 5-minute candle closed above the 21 EMA with rising volume or momentum - one of the board's 30 biggest stocks. Bot 2 weeks (calls): lost money

docs.title: Gap reclaim (calls)
docs.text: RECLAIM↑: gapped DOWN below yesterday's low, then the first 5-minute candle closed back ABOVE it. Bot 2 weeks: lost money

docs.title: Daily line $100 (calls)
docs.text: $LINE↑: the daily line on $100+ stocks only - opened $100+ above yesterday's high with $0.50 of room to the next daily line, 5m closed above the 21 EMA with rising volume or momentum

docs.title: MOM strong (filled) (calls)
docs.text: MOM↑ with the CYAN FILL: the 5-minute squeeze-momentum line is above 0 and rising (buying getting stronger) AND the trend is strong on 5m and 30m (+DI above 25 and above -DI). The only MOM↑ the Setup column shows

docs.title: MOM (any) (calls)
docs.text: Every MOM↑, filled or not: the 5-minute squeeze-momentum line is cyan - above 0 and rising - on today's candle. The outlined (not strong) ones are hidden in the Setup column but still pass here

docs.title: AI score 55%+ (test) (calls)
docs.text: AI 61%: the highest shadow model score among this ticker's recorded call paper trades today, shown from 55%. The Record tooltip identifies the trade and model. This describes an earlier paper trade, not a calibrated win probability for the current setup. Profitability after trading costs has not been established

docs.title: 🔥 Chart squeeze (calls)
docs.text: 🔥1h 2h 09:00: the CHART's squeeze flame - the same 🔥 your chart draws (Cloud_Signal_Squeeze) on the 1h, 2h, 4h or Daily candle that started at that time, premarket included, on the forming candle like TOS. Shown for one candle of its timeframe; ✕ = the chart removed it. A different script from the scanner's SQZ column (Squeeze410), so the two can fire at different times. Not back-tested

docs.title: ⚡ setup fired (calls)
docs.text: ⚡ (first in the cell): one of the main setups fired today - GO, GO+ or MX A+. It flashes for 10 minutes when new; the setup's own tag is in the same cell

docs.title: ⭐1 (calls)
docs.text: ⭐1: the #1 of today's best setups, ranked in your tested order - GO inside a hot or moving sector first, then other GO, then OPT (first seen before 10:00); fewer warnings rank higher. Bot 2 weeks: about -4% (bull) / +5% (bear) ROI at middle price

docs.title: 🔥 / 🔸 SECTOR (calls)
docs.text: 🔥 SECTOR: this stock is a leader of one of today's two HOT sectors (latched 09:35-11:00). 🔸 SECTOR: a leader of a sector moving now. The sector's stocks are up and above VWAP together. Bot 2 weeks: hot +0%, moving +6% ROI at middle price

docs.title: ZS (calls)
docs.text: ZS↑ (time = when it first fired today): a 5-minute candle closed ABOVE the EMA 9, 21 and 50, VWAP and the 5m cloud, with nothing in the way within 2% above (day high, premarket high, yesterday's high, pivots). Bot 2 weeks: +7% ROI at middle price, small

docs.title: ⚠ Warning (calls)
docs.text: ⚠ Careful: the row shows a setup, but also a pattern seen behind wrong picks - momentum fading, below VWAP, already up 8%+, 30m sellers in control, or bad news. The tag lists which

docs.title: 💥 Explosive pattern (calls)
docs.text: 💥 Explosive (shown beside the grade letter): a sudden burst of buying - one of the last 6 five-minute candles traded 3+ times its usual volume swing and closed in its upper half, while the 5m breakout is confirmed or holding. Big money stepped in; the move may already have run. Bot: tracked from Oct 12, not tested yet

docs.title: 📈 Steady pattern (calls)
docs.text: 📈 Steady (shown beside the grade letter): a slow, clean climb - at least 4 of the last 6 fifteen-minute candles made a higher high and a higher low, with the price above the 20 EMA. An orderly trend. Bot: tracked from Oct 12, not tested yet

docs.title: FLIP (calls)
docs.text: FLIP↑: on the last closed 5-minute candle the trend background flipped from sellers to buyers (+DI crossed above -DI) while the momentum dots are rising. Earlier than MOM↑

docs.title: RVOL tag (calls)
